_comment: A non-React motion reel that must pass every motion grader: the TLB, from content/session_18_paging.md section 3.4. Guards against rules that only a React/code topic can satisfy. The material has no code, so no shot shows code and the code_map is a card of parts. break_2 is omitted (10 shots) because the material states one reason. Also the stub answer for SYSTEM_MOTION when the material teaches the TLB.
topic: Why does address translation need the TLB?
hook_question: Why does every memory lookup feel twice as slow?

shots.speech: Why does every memory lookup feel twice as slow?
shots.visual: Terminal mock running a program; every memory read goes out twice; status pill 'Slow'.

shots.speech: One small cache fixes this. Here is how.
shots.visual: Title card: series label, 'TLB', the promise line, three icon tiles.

shots.speech: Your program asks for one address. The page table says which frame holds that page.
shots.visual: Entity card 'Program' asking for an address; system panel 'Page table' with rows of page -> frame.

shots.speech: But the page table lives in memory too. So every lookup first reads the table, then the data.
shots.visual: Two pulses leave the entity card for memory on every lookup: one to the table, one to the data.

shots.speech: Meet the TLB, a small cache. It keeps recent page to frame answers close by.
shots.visual: A system panel 'TLB' appears beside the entity card holding three recent page -> frame slots.

shots.speech: On a TLB hit, the frame number is ready at once. You skip the table walk.
shots.visual: Trigger chip 'lookup page 5' pulses to the TLB panel; the slot lights; the frame number returns without touching the page table.

shots.speech: Each entry maps a page number to a frame number. A miss walks the table once, then saves it.
shots.visual: Code map card: page number -> grid icon 'which page'; frame number -> memory icon 'where it lives'; miss -> bolt icon 'walk once, then cache'.

shots.speech: Now the same lookup reads memory once, and your program runs fast.
shots.visual: The hook's terminal mock again: one memory read per lookup; status pill 'Fast'.

shots.speech: Remember: the page table lives in memory. The TLB caches recent answers. A hit skips the walk.
shots.visual: Takeaway list: three rows with the grid, memory and bolt icons.

shots.speech: Follow for more, one idea at a time.
shots.visual: End card: Up next, Follow button, series chips.
